construction.access_recipe: Download the publisher raw text file with source_io.fetch from https://primis.phmsa.dot.gov/enforcement-documents/PHMSA%20Pipeline%20Enforcement%20Raw%20Data.txt. The file is not pure UTF-8: decode the downloaded bytes with utf-8-sig first and fall back to cp1252 (then latin-1), recording the encoding that succeeded and asserting zero U+FFFD replacement characters. Parse the decoded text with pandas read_csv from an in-memory buffer using sep=chr(9), quotechar=chr(34), dtype=str, keep_default_na=False and engine='python'. Resolve raw header names case-insensitively with punctuation stripped; the current 53-field header carries CPF_Number (the operator case number, not CPF), WMS_Activity_Seq, Case_Type, Notice_Sent_Date, Proposed_Penalties, Assessed_Penalties, Closed_Date, Violation_Category, Cited_Regulations, Pipeline_Type, Region, How_Discovered? (question mark retained by the publisher), Notice_Actions and Proposed_Compliance_Order_Ind. Keep rows whose Case_Type denotes a Notice of Probable Violation, keep a present and strictly positive Proposed_Penalties, keep a parseable Notice_Sent_Date in 2002-01-01 through 2023-06-30, and deduplicate to the earliest notice per WMS_Activity_Seq. Count list tokens in Violation_Category and distinct tokens in Cited_Regulations. Assign penalty_reduced a value of one when Closed_Date is no later than 36 months after Notice_Sent_Date and Assessed_Penalties is present and strictly below Proposed_Penalties; otherwise use zero. Do not use Assessed_Penalties or Closed_Date as features.
construction.expected_size: Observed 1,977,064 characters and 53 columns in the current raw text file; estimated 3,000–5,000 total case rows from average row length, with the eligible NOPV-with-positive-proposed-penalty subset expected in the high hundreds to low thousands across 2002–2026.
construction.format: Tab-delimited UTF-8 text with a header row and quoted fields containing commas.
construction.source_examples: CPF 32026008NOPV: INTERSTATE LIQUID, Proposed_Penalties=228200, Assessed_Penalties=228200, Final_Order_Date=9/8/26. CPF 32026011NOPV: Proposed_Penalties=532030, Assessed_Penalties=207100, Consent_Order_Date=9/30/26. CPF 12026035NOPV: Proposed_Penalties=72200, Assessed_Penalties=59500, Closed_Date=9/9/26. CPF 52026007NOPV: Proposed_Penalties blank and Closed_Date=10/13/26, illustrating the positive-proposed-penalty filter.

limitations: Current-vintage retrospective extract as of 2026-11-03; historical fields may have been updated after case closure, so this does not prove the exact feature set was operationally available to an earlier decision-maker.

Right-censoring: cases not closed with a reduction within 36 months are coded 0, so later reductions are missed; closed cases with missing Assessed_Penalties are also coded 0 and may hide administrative eliminations recorded as blanks.
Selection: only NOPVs with positive proposed penalties are eligible; warning letters, notices of amendment, corrective action orders, and compliance-only cases are excluded.
Cases cluster by operator and sometimes share an inspection; no operator history or lagged outcome features are used, but evaluation should account for operator clustering.
The data dictionary is dated 2023 and uses some field names that differ from the 2026 raw header; construction must follow the raw header and map semantics explicitly.
No causal interpretation: inspection routes, regions, and case initiation reflect PHMSA enforcement selection and legal process, not random assignment.

The U.S. public-domain basis is territorial; 17 U.S.C. § 105 does not establish a worldwide dedication, and reuse outside the United States may depend on local law. No third-party photo or document rights are included.
reason: PHMSA publishes a directly downloadable, documented tab-delimited extract of pipeline enforcement cases spanning 2002–2026, with a notice-stage proposed penalty and a later assessed-penalty outcome. This supports a clean binary prediction task with fixed chronological splits, no accounts, and no joins. PHMSA's public-information policy and 17 U.S.C. § 105 support U.S. redistribution, subject to explicit territorial limits.

features.name: proposed_penalty_usd

features.meaning: Number of nonempty comma-separated violation categories in Violation_Category.
features.name: violation_category_count

features.availability: Derived only from regulations cited in Cited_Regulations at notice; blank remains missing.
features.meaning: Number of distinct nonempty regulation codes in Cited_Regulations.
features.name: cited_regulation_count

features.availability: Derived from whether Violation_Category contains Integrity Management at notice; blank remains missing.
features.name: integrity_management_flag

features.availability: Recorded on the case at notice; current-vintage extract; historical availability assumed.

features.availability: Recorded on the case at notice; current-vintage extract; historical availability assumed.

task.outcome_horizon: 36 months after Notice_Sent_Date; holdout notices end 2023-06-30, so all outcomes are observable by 2026-06-30 against the 2026-11-03 extract
task.population: NOPV cases with positive Proposed_Penalties and nonmissing Notice_Sent_Date from 2002-01-01 through 2023-06-30; deduplicated to earliest NOPV per WMS_Activity_Seq. Eligibility uses only decision-time information.
task.prediction_time: Notice_Sent_Date, before the operator response, hearing or any order.
task.question: Will a PHMSA Notice of Probable Violation with a proposed civil penalty be closed within 36 months with a lower assessed penalty than proposed?
task.simple_references: Majority class; logistic regression using log(1 + proposed_penalty_usd) alone; calendar-year base rate. No persistence baseline is appropriate because cases are not a regularly sampled time series.
task.split_policy: Fixed chronological boundaries by Notice_Sent_Date: train 2002-01-01 to 2016-12-31; evaluation 2017-01-01 to 2019-12-31; holdout 2020-01-01 to 2023-06-30. No embargo is needed because no lagged outcomes, rolling histories, operator histories, or future case records are used; related cases are deduplicated by WMS_Activity_Seq before splitting.
task.target: y=1 iff the case has a nonmissing Closed_Date no later than 36 months after Notice_Sent_Date and Assessed_Penalties is nonmissing and strictly less than Proposed_Penalties (zero counts as elimination); otherwise y=0, including cases not closed with a reduction by 36 months. Closed cases with missing Assessed_Penalties are coded 0, not imputed.
task.usefulness: The proposed demand is known at notice, but the final assessment is not; the task tests whether violation mix, enforcement channel, pipeline segment and proposed amount predict whether PHMSA demand is discounted. It is not a copied status field and supports contest-versus-negotiate triage.

title: Will PHMSA's proposed pipeline-safety civil penalty be reduced or eliminated within 36 months?
